_metadata.description: Unit conversion factors for supplement dosing normalization

statistics.notes: DSLD is supplement-only: beta-carotene uses the supplemental rule; alpha-carotene and beta-cryptoxanthin use the NIH 24:1 RAE factor; choline bitartrate uses its verified 1:1 salt stoichiometry; CFU parsing is owned by enrichment; bare folate preserves unknown form lineage; explicit DFE units normalize without assuming folic acid; parent Vitamin E amounts declared in mg use the FDA alpha-tocopherol label basis

_metadata.total_entries_note: Count of vitamin_conversions rules; mass_conversions has 6 rules and form_detection_patterns has 2 vitamin patterns

vitamin_d3.notes: FDA requires mcg on labels since 2020; IU may appear in parentheses

vitamin_e_d_alpha_tocopherol.notes: Natural form has higher bioavailability than synthetic

vitamin_e_dl_alpha_tocopherol.notes: Synthetic form - approximately 50% bioavailability of natural

warnings: UL of 3000 mcg RAE applies to preformed vitamin A only
Pregnant women should not exceed 3000 mcg RAE
High doses may increase fracture risk

vitamin_a_beta_carotene_supplement.notes: Beta-carotene from supplements has no established UL; body regulates conversion

vitamin_a_other_provitamin_a_carotenoid.notes: NIH defines 24 mcg alpha-carotene or beta-cryptoxanthin as 1 mcg RAE. The preformed-vitamin-A UL does not apply.
vitamin_a_other_provitamin_a_carotenoid.source: NIH ODS Vitamin A and Carotenoids Fact Sheet for Health Professionals

vitamin_a_unknown.notes: If vitamin A form cannot be determined, flag product for manual review
warnings: Cannot safely convert without knowing form - retinol vs beta-carotene matters for UL

choline_bitartrate_to_choline.notes: Active-moiety factor is choline molecular weight 104.17 divided by anhydrous 1:1 choline bitartrate molecular weight 253.25.
choline_bitartrate_to_choline.source: FDA GSRS UNII 6K2W7T9V6Y; NIH PubChem CID 6900 and CID 305

vitamin_e_unknown.notes: If vitamin E form cannot be determined, flag for review. Do NOT default to the synthetic 0.45 mg/IU factor - it under-states mg vs natural 0.67 mg/IU and can hide an over-UL dose.
warnings: Cannot safely convert without knowing form - natural (d-alpha) 0.67 vs synthetic (dl-alpha) 0.45 mg/IU

vitamin_e_label_mg_alpha_tocopherol.notes: A Supplement Facts parent nutrient amount headed Vitamin E and declared in mg uses the FDA mg alpha-tocopherol label basis. This rule does not apply to legacy IU or standalone mixed-tocopherol/tocotrienol masses.
vitamin_e_label_mg_alpha_tocopherol.source: FDA guidance: Converting Units of Measure for Folate, Niacin, and Vitamins A, D, and E on Nutrition and Supplement Facts Labels

folate_unknown.notes: Preserve label-declared DFE for adequacy, but do not infer a synthetic folic-acid contribution for UL assessment.
warnings: Cannot apply the synthetic folic-acid UL without explicit form lineage
folate_unknown.source: FDA folate labeling guidance; NIH ODS Folate Fact Sheet

folate_folic_acid.notes: Folic acid on empty stomach: 1 mcg = 1.7 mcg DFE; with food: 1 mcg = 1 mcg DFE

folate_methylfolate.notes: Active form - same DFE conversion as folic acid

niacin.notes: NE = Niacin Equivalents; 60 mg tryptophan = 1 mg NE. Preformed niacin (nicotinic acid / niacinamide) is 1:1 with NE in both directions, so a label printed in mg NE compares directly against a mg niacin threshold; the 60:1 tryptophan factor applies to dietary protein only, never to a niacin ingredient row.

vitamin_k1.notes: No IU conversion - always measured in mcg

vitamin_k2.notes: No IU conversion - always measured in mcg; MK-7 has longer half-life than MK-4

vitamin_b12.notes: No IU conversion - measured in mcg; forms include cyanocobalamin (most common), methylcobalamin (active), adenosylcobalamin

selenium.notes: No IU conversion - measured in mcg; forms include selenomethionine, sodium selenite, sodium selenate

chromium.notes: No IU conversion - measured in mcg; picolinate form most common in supplements

biotin.notes: No IU conversion - measured in mcg; also known as vitamin H or vitamin B7

iodine.notes: No IU conversion - measured in mcg; common forms include potassium iodide and kelp-derived

molybdenum.notes: No IU conversion - measured in mcg

form_detection_patterns._description: Regex patterns to detect vitamin forms from ingredient names

vitamin_e.notes: If form cannot be determined, assume synthetic (conservative)

vitamin_a.notes: Explicit beta-carotene gets the supplemental beta-carotene factor. Explicit alpha-carotene and beta-cryptoxanthin use the NIH 24:1 RAE factor. Generic carotenoid or provitamin-A labels remain form-unknown; do not default (UL implications).
